MT5 MCP Bridge & Decision Trace

This page documents the work merged in #676 — after the v9.0.17 release, so unreleased until the next tag. Everything below is enforcement in code with a regression test, not a roadmap item.

مهم

The MCP transport is read-only. It cannot place, modify or close an

order, and it is off by default. Enabling it does not change how the

engine talks to MetaTrader 5 — only code that explicitly constructs

MCPMT5Adapter uses it.

Why a second transport exists

Before this wave the repository had no MCP client at all: a raw grep for 22346 | MCPToolbox | mcp_client across src/, scripts/, tests/ and configs/ returned zero hits, while a 66-tool terminal bridge was running on the same box. The engine's read surface was therefore unreachable from anything but the native Win32 IPC adapter or the ZMQ gateway.

adapters/mt5/mcp_adapter.py closes that gap by implementing the read surface of IMT5Port over the local MCP endpoint (HTTP JSON-RPC, protocol 2025-06-18), returning the same typed snapshots the native adapter produces — build_account_snapshot / build_symbol_snapshot are reused directly, so downstream consumers cannot tell which transport answered.

Tools consumed (verified live, all read-only):

text
get_trading_account_info      get_marketwatch_symbols
get_chart_history             get_chart_ticks_history
get_trading_open_positions    get_trading_history_orders
get_trading_history_positions get_time_information
get_workspace_info            get_terminal_journal

Read-only by construction

GuardBehaviour
FORBIDDEN_TOOLS frozensetBlocks the whole trade_* surface at the transport boundary — a future caller cannot reach a mutating tool even by accident
Port write methodssend_order, execute_market_order, place_pending_order, modify_position, close_position, modify_order, cancel_pending_order raise NotImplementedError without issuing any MCP call
connect()Raises on transport or auth failure — never returns False silently
Read failuresSurface as available=False + an error_state snapshot; values are never fabricated
History windowsRange-only: datetime_from / datetime_to are required, a future datetime_to is rejected by the bridge, so count-based port methods derive the range from the terminal clock and record the clamp in the snapshot note
Empty windowok:true + history:[] is a legitimate empty result, logged at debug — not an error

Credentials follow the same contract as the remote gateway: NSE_MT5_MCP_URL and NSE_MT5_MCP_API_KEY from the environment (or the repo-root .env), sent only as X-API-Key / Authorization. The key is never logged, never stringified into an exception and never returned from a method.

Enabling it

yaml
# configs/base.yaml
mt5:
  mcp:
    enabled: false        # default: byte-identical behaviour for everyone else
    url: ""               # empty -> NSE_MT5_MCP_URL from env / .env
    read_only: true       # documents the intent; enforcement lives in the adapter
    timeout_s: 60.0
bash
export NSE_MT5_MCP_URL="http://127.0.0.1:22346/mcp"
export NSE_MT5_MCP_API_KEY="…"   # environment only — never in a config file

Causal trace emission

observability/trace_mt5_emit.py turns a real broker result object into the frozen v2 causal field dict. It is duck-typed on purpose (no isinstance on adapter classes, no imports of them), so it stays importable from any context:

  • direct MT5 order_send / order_check → retcode, order, deal, price, volume, comment
  • remote-gateway RPC response → status, message, ticket, order_id, deal_id
  • paper adapter → success + the internal simulated ticket (gateway="paper", simulated=True)

trace_contract.sanitize_detail redacts secrets at the boundary before an event is stored, so an API key or an account credential cannot reach the ring, a log line or an SSE frame.

Trace routes

The observer is a passive in-memory store; the routes only read it. No handler touches the trading engine, and an exception in a handler can never reach the engine — every route is guarded and returns an honest error payload.

EndpointPurpose
GET /api/trace/observerObserver status: session, schema version, ring occupancy
POST /api/trace/observer/start · /stopStart / stop collection
GET /api/trace/topologyNode + edge view of the decision path
GET /api/trace/latencyPer-stage latency samples
GET /api/trace/integrityChain/sequence integrity report
GET /api/trace/decisionsDecision events
GET /api/trace/eventsRaw events (bounded batch)
GET /api/trace/bundle/{key}Evidence bundle for one correlation key
GET /api/trace/why/{event_id}The WHY chain for a single event
GET /api/trace/streamSSE stream: hello, batch, heartbeat, error

The stream resumes explicitly: the client sends ?last_seq= on reconnect. If the ring has already evicted that point the batch carries gap: true, and the UI is required to render TRACE GAP instead of implying continuity.

Replay identity gate

POST /api/replay/session requires a dataset_fingerprint (8–64 chars). The records loader is the authority on dataset identity: if the requested id and fingerprint do not describe the dataset it loaded, it raises DatasetIdentityError and the route answers 422 with rejection: "dataset_identity".

That is a deliberate, fail-closed rejection — not a server fault. It is the difference between "this run is not comparable" and a silent comparison across two different datasets. Every other failure returns the generic error envelope with no str(e) on the wire (the text can name an internal artifact path); the full detail goes to the server log only.

Honest /system diagnostics (F-22)

An adapter that cannot report diagnostics used to degrade to mt5: null — indistinguishable from "no adapter attached", which the live-state route then rendered as available: true with an empty diagnostics dict. A false green.

json
{ "mt5": { "available": false, "reason": "DIAGNOSTICS_UNAVAILABLE",
           "detail": "adapter.diagnostics_summary() raised RuntimeError" } }
{ "mt5": { "available": false, "reason": "NO_ADAPTER_ATTACHED" } }

Bounded runtime memory (H-04 / H-05)

Two structures used to grow with uptime; both are now capped, so a long SHADOW/PAPER run cannot exhaust the process:

  • H-04 — the paper ledger is bounded (no unbounded fill history).
  • H-05 — the completed-bar ring is bounded (no unbounded bar retention).

Verification

SuiteWhat it pins
tests/unit/test_mcp_adapter_contract.pyRead-only invariants, forbidden-tool refusal, envelope mapping, redaction
tests/unit/test_trace_mt5_emit.pyFrozen v2 causal fields per result shape, secret redaction
tests/unit/test_replay_routes_contract.pyIdentity gate (422), error envelopes, no internals on the wire
tests/unit/test_mt5_memory_bounds.pyH-04 / H-05 caps under sustained load
tests/integration/test_mcp_adapter_live_readonly.pyLive bridge, skipped unless the MCP env contract is present

Merge gate for #676: ruff + format clean, mypy src with a byte-identical error set versus the pre-merge baseline, dependency drift and migration safety OK, and 168 passed / 31 skipped / 0 failed across the recovered and regression suites (every skip named an environment or data guard).

Status

CapabilityGradeNote
MCP read adapterIMPLEMENTEDOff by default; read-only enforced at the transport boundary
MCP trade/write pathNOT BUILT — by designtrade_* tools are blocked, not proxied
Trace emission + observerIMPLEMENTEDBounded ring, redaction, SSE resume with explicit gaps
Replay identity gateIMPLEMENTEDFails closed on a mismatched dataset
Bounded memory (H-04/H-05)IMPLEMENTEDCaps covered by regression tests
